title: What Lunar Internet Systems Is
definition: Lunar Internet Systems: internet infrastructure for the Moon.
description:

t: Real Research Today: Lunar Internet Systems
title: Real Research Today: Lunar Internet Systems
definition: Today's documented research behind Lunar Internet Systems.
description:
The road to Lunar Internet Systems is already being paved. Meta's EMG wristband and Neuralink's implants advance neural input devices. Ultrasonic mid-air haptics (Ultraleap) create touchable interfaces from sound.

Animal communication AI (Project CETI on sperm whales, Earth Species Project) decodes nonhuman signals. Together these programs form the relay orbiters foundation that Lunar Internet Systems will build on — the lunar logistics results, the delay tolerance methods, and the institutional memory.

Forecasts are projections, not promises: the dated milestones in this database reflect published roadmaps and expert surveys, and they will move as lunar logistics research advances. Treat every date as a planning scenario with error bars, and watch the signals listed in each milestone record.

title: 2030 — First consumer lunar hulls terminals ship: relay orbiters input

description:
First consumer lunar hulls terminals ship: relay orbiters input plus lunar logistics output in one wearable.

What must be true first: the relay orbiters results have to replicate outside the lab, lunar logistics manufacturing must reach pilot scale, and delay tolerance operations need a year of continuous runtime. Miss any one and the date slips — that is the honest mechanics of forecasting.

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed relay orbiters demonstrations, lunar logistics cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting delay tolerance uptime. When all three flash green, 2030 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (4 years from the 2026 baseline.)

title: Readiness Estimator: Lunar Internet Systems
definition: Estimates Lunar Internet Systems readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Lunar Internet Systems components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a lunar hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Lunar Internet Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Lunar Internet Systems operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Lunar Internet Systems installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 5096 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where relay orbiters monitoring, lunar logistics redundancy, or delay tolerance maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Lunar Internet Systems Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Lunar Internet Systems: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Lunar Internet Systems — internet infrastructure for the Moon.

Phase 1 — Prove (relay orbiters): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (lunar logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (delay tolerance): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (surface mesh): lunar hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and Moon-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
